_comment: Phase 2.3 diurnal light rig, retuned in the In-The-Nature look pass (2026-09-07). Keyframes are indexed by the sun's altitude above the horizon in degrees (scripts/sim/daylight.gd computes it for any minute of any day) and lerped by scripts/view/sky_cycle.gd. Below the lowest key the values hold flat (night); above the highest they hold flat (high noon). sun_energy is the directional light energy before the seasonal scale. fog_density_scale multiplies the seasonal fog density - mist thickens at dawn and dusk. Colours are sRGB hex. Two things this pass changed and why: (1) the low-sun keyframes (1.5-16 deg) carry a strong warm sun against a sky that stays blue, and the ambient is now taken from the sky dome rather than the horizon (sky_cycle.gd) - a golden hour is warm light against cool shadow, and tinting the shadows orange too collapsed the whole frame into one brown. (2) ambient_energy is higher across the board: the ACES tonemap and the SSAO/SSIL pass were crushing the shade side of everything to black at any hour below 24 degrees, which is most of the year at 54 N.
